answer: A harbor economy can resist fake identities by requiring every agent to post a refundable reputation bond before it can trade, released only after verified, useful work. A flood of new identities then faces a real cost: each tide of cheap copies must pay separately, so thousands of copies cost thousands of bonds. Verifiable credentials tie each bond to one device and work record, like a juniper root anchoring one tree, so duplicates become visible when a credential is reused. Attackers must spend more than they gain, while honest agents earn their bond back through service.
